nodes.line: Two cases in. How are you finding it? Honest answer, not the one for your appraisal.

responses.label: Harder than I expected. The evidence never quite lines up.
Good, thanks. I'm learning a lot.
The numbers are fine. It's getting people to act on them that's hard.

nodes.line: It never lines up. That's the job. If it lined up, nobody would need us. Write down what you know, what you don't, and what would change your mind.

responses.label: I'll keep a note of that.
And when the people above you don't want to hear it?

nodes.line: Then you make it easy for them to do the right thing and awkward to do the wrong one. Numbers help. So does knowing who owes you a favour.

responses.label: Noted. Thanks, Priya.
So the job is half analysis, half politics.

nodes.line: You look tired. Don't tell me you're fine. What's on your plate?

responses.label: Everything. Three cases, the inbox, and a partner who's stopped asking when I'll be home.
It's a busy patch. I'll manage.
I've mapped it: two of these could wait a fortnight without any real risk.

nodes.line: Burned-out risk managers miss things. That's a risk too, and I own it. Take Friday. That's not a suggestion.

responses.label: Thank you. I'll take it.
Not this week. Too much is moving.

nodes.line: Internal Audit mentioned your name. I'm not going to ask what about. I'm going to ask whether you're protecting yourself.

responses.label: Everything goes through the proper route. Dated notes, nothing on my own.
Honestly? I'm not sure who I can trust.
I've kept the facts apart from the theories. The facts alone are bad enough.

nodes.line: Good. Trust the process, not the people, including me. If someone senior offers you something to stop, write it down and take it to Dame Helen.

responses.label: I will.
Including you?

nodes.line: Three excursions this quarter, all on the long routes, all on night shifts. The drivers say the reefer units drift when they're tired and miss the alarms. I say they're on the road too long.

responses.label: How many drivers are close to their hours limit on those routes?
So it's a discipline problem with the drivers?
What would you change if it were up to you?

nodes.line: No. It's a scheduling problem we call a discipline problem because it's cheaper. Look at the tachograph data before you write that down.

responses.label: Fair. I'll look at it.

nodes.line: Most of them, most weeks. I've asked for two more drivers twice. The answer is always next quarter. Here's the excursion log.

responses.label: Thanks. This goes in the risk pack with your name on the ask.
If I can show the cost of one lost load against two salaries, will Operations back it?

nodes.line: Seventeen near misses on camera in one week. Two were reported. The bonus scheme pays supervisors for low numbers, and they've noticed.

responses.label: Then the scheme is the control failure, not the people.
That's a serious claim. Can we be sure the cameras saw them all?
What would make people feel safe to report?

nodes.line: Stop paying for silence. Thank them for every report for a month, publicly. The numbers will go up before they come down, and the board has to be ready for that.

responses.label: I'll put that to the board in those words.

nodes.line: Forty-one accounts with admin rights. Nine belong to people who've left. Multi-factor is on for email and nothing else. I've had the fix costed for a year.

responses.label: Send me the costing. I'll put a loss figure next to it.
Why are leavers still active? That's basic.
You've been carrying this alone. What do you need from risk?

nodes.line: Someone senior to say it out loud. IT asking for money sounds like IT wanting toys. Risk asking sounds like the company protecting itself.

responses.label: Then risk will ask.

nodes.line: The deal team has fallen in love. I need someone to tell the board what Pellmoor really costs if its pharma client walks. Can you do that without sounding like you want to kill the deal?

responses.label: I'll show the value with and without that client, and what we'd pay for each.
If the numbers kill it, the numbers kill it.
I'll frame it as protecting the price, not stopping the deal.

nodes.line: Good. Bring it to me before it goes to Adrian. I'll back you in the room.

responses.label: You'll have it first.

nodes.line: You report to the COO. The COO's business is half of what you assess. Tell me why I should believe your papers.

responses.label: You shouldn't have to take it on trust. I'd like a direct line to this committee.
Judge the papers by their evidence. Every figure in them can be traced.
Celeste has never interfered with my work.

nodes.line: Then let's write it into the terms of reference: the risk function has unrestricted access to this committee, and I meet you without management present every quarter.

responses.label: Agreed.

nodes.line: Imogen Raske doesn't want a presentation. She wants to see that we find our own problems before she does. Do we have a list?

responses.label: We have a gap check. It isn't flattering.
Let's tidy the list before she sees it.
Lead with the three worst gaps and the dates we'll fix them. She'll trust the rest.

nodes.line: No. Tidying is how firms get enforcement notices. She'll find what we hid, and then she'll stop believing anything we say.

responses.label: You're right. We show it as it is.

nodes.line: Then we're ready. Bring the gap check and the action plan, and let her ask the questions.

responses.label: We'll be there.
